I fixed the 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. After the fixes, all 150 rules give the same results as their docstrings and the module docstring's common rules.

**What I fixed**

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 01, 28 | Discount was 13% instead of 12% | `* 12 // 100` |
| 07 | A "whole" rule computed the discount like a "marginal" rule, only on units above the threshold | `base * 8 // 100` |
| 42 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount (`min(base, 10000) * 5%`) | Take 5% of the full price, then cap the discount at 10,000 won |
| 53, 64, 150 | Used `round()`, so amounts were rounded instead of floored to the won | Changed to `//` |
| 60, 132 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won, so discounts between 30,000 and 60,000 won weren't capped | Always apply `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 124 | At exactly the threshold (12 units) there was no discount (`qty > 12`) | `qty >= 12` |
| 148 | At exactly the threshold (100 units) there was no discount (`qty > 100`) | `qty >= 100` |

Rule 72 also uses `qty > 100`, but I left it unchanged. It's a marginal rule, so the discount at exactly 100 units is 0 either way and the result is the same.

**How I checked:** I wrote a reference calculator from each docstring's type, percentage, threshold and cap. I compared it with every rule over quantities 0–259 plus a few large values, and 18 unit prices including 0 and large numbers. The check also confirms that negative inputs raise `ValueError`. Before the fixes, the check reported exactly these 11 rules. After them, it reports 0 mismatches. The check script and the original file are saved in `/tmp/chk/`.

STATUS: DONE
